DIAGNOSIS READY: Breastfeeding Jaundice (Physiological Jaundice of the Breastfed Infant)

The clinical picture of unconjugated hyperbilirubinemia peaking at day 5 in a healthy, full-term infant exclusively breastfed without signs of dehydration or infection is classic for this condition. The total bilirubin level of 14.2 mg/dL is below the phototherapy threshold for a 5-day-old at this weight/age, so we can continue breastfeeding frequently to maintain hydration and promote stooling to lower bilirubin levels. No further imaging or tests are required at this time.
